newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: D&B credit rating for Slovenia steady at DB3a.
newsitem.headline: D&B credit rating for Slovenia steady at DB3a.

text.p: Slovenia's March credit rating remains unchanged at DB3a after the country managed to resolve more than three months of political deadlock, credit rating agency Dun and Bradstreet (D&B) said on Thursday.

On February 27, parliament approved the new government led by Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek. The cabinet was formed as a coalition of Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats with the conservative People's Party and Desus, the pensioners' party.

Although the vote took place more than three months after inconclusive November 10 general election, the agency awarded Slovenia an unchanged rating for the ninth month in a row, ranking it behind the Czech Republic and ahead of Poland.
"Slovenia's economy continues to remain largely unaffected by such political wrangling," the agency said in its latest Risk & Payment Review, published in Ljubljana.

The agency said it remained concerned about a central bank regulation which forces foreign investors to open custodian trading accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licenced banks if they want to trade in Slovenian securities.
The announcement caused a 17.4 percent fall in the SBI share index as international investors pulled the plug on Slovenian securities. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
